title: What is the best way to generate Morse code signals on an STM32?
content:
I’m looking into implementing Morse code output on an STM32 using a buzzer and LED. The main thing I’m trying to figure out is how to handle the timing for dots, dashes, and gaps accurately, especially when allowing different WPM speeds.

Would you recommend using a hardware timer/PWM, a timer interrupt, or another approach?

I’m also looking for a simple way to test the generated Morse sequences before sending them to the hardware. I’ve been using this online Morse translator as a reference for converting and checking Morse sequences:

For example, if the STM32 receives "SOS", I’d like it to generate:

... --- ...

What would be the cleanest implementation approach on STM32?

scraped_replies.html: Much the same as for any other microcontroller: have a timer set up for dot, dash, inter-word pause, etc ...

>What would be the cleanest implementation approach on STM32?

I’d say: exactly same as on other cpu/SOC .

ymmv.

So many options how to do this…

Morse code at human readable / audible speed?

If yes, I suppose a few milliseconds error is no problem, so I’d built a state machine and use the SysTick for timing.
